correctness.rationale: The graph is connected, simple, bipartite, both vertex- and edge-transitive, with degree at least three. Total unimodularity establishes every defining facet. The spectral trace equation has a unique root by a monotone positive eigenvalue sum and strict endpoint inequalities. Facet-support identities are exact consequences of trace and transitivity, and positive contact weights establish both John moment identities. Extremal signless-Laplacian eigenvalues and its exact second trace moment prove the condition number and high-degree limit. Thirteen graph instances and 893 facet norms were checked numerically as corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact target is all connected, degree-at-least-three, vertex/edge-transitive bipartite graph stable-set polytopes. Search of archived own claim titles, published mathematical records and full primary texts found previously treated complete bicliques and fractional matching polytopes, but not the encompassing stable-set spectral formula or universal high-degree eccentricity theorem. Complete bicliques and degree-two line-graph cases are not counted as new. A general transposed-incidence theorem remains a bibliographic risk.
